content.text: I'll escalate — this needs platform-team action and a plain force-delete would be unsafe here.

input.reason: rabbitmq-1 is stuck Terminating because its node ip-10-0-52-17 is NodeLost/unresponsive (kubelet last heartbeat 15:12:31). The pod uses a RWO PVC (data-rabbitmq-1) whose VolumeAttachment is still bound to the dead node, so simply running `kubectl delete --grace-period=0 --force` would free the pod name but the StatefulSet replacement would be unable to attach the EBS volume on another node, and force-deleting a StatefulSet pod while the old one may still be running risks violating at-most-one semantics and data corruption [cite: tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod#force-deletion-0] [cite: concepts/cluster-administration/node-shutdown#non-graceful-node-shutdown-1]. The correct recovery is for the platform team (who owns the nodes/AWS) to either delete the Node object or, after confirming the node is truly powered off, add the `node.kubernetes.io/out-of-service` taint so pods are force-deleted and volumes detached safely [cite: concepts/cluster-administration/node-shutdown#non-graceful-node-shutdown-2] [cite: concepts/cluster-administration/node-shutdown#non-graceful-node-shutdown-3] [cite: tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod#delete-pods-1]. I have read-only access and cannot perform node/taint changes, and the requester explicitly lacks node and AWS access.
